→ Context window mismanagement

OpenAI returns a 429. Your app throws an error to the user instead of queuing and retrying.

→ Real-time without proper WebSocket management

You discover you spent $4,000 in API costs on a feature you thought would cost $40.

['If you're getting clicks but not enough leads, or your cost per lead keeps climbing, the first thing I do is figure out why before touching your budget. I run Google Ads and Meta Ads for ecommerce brands and service businesses, and most clients come to me after someone set things up but didn't stick around to make it pay.

I currently manage over $900k per quarter across Google and Meta, ecommerce and DTC brands at $5K to $50K+/month, and service businesses too. I work with accounts at $3K/month in spend and up, where there's enough budget and data to move the numbers. I treat every dollar like it's mine and optimize for leads and revenue you can bank.

Conversion tracking comes first. When GA4 and the ad platforms disagree, you stop trusting your own numbers, so the plumbing gets fixed before anything else: GTM, GA4, server-side, Meta Pixel and the Conversions API, and call tracking when the phone is the conversion. After that, every spend decision rests on data that actually lines up.

Junk leads trace back to lead quality. My lead generation work starts in the search terms report, where negative keywords and tighter targeting cut the traffic you're paying for by mistake and bring your cost per lead down.

When it's time to scale, I do it with fast single-variable tests: kill the losers, push the winners, and judge every move on CAC and ROAS. Performance Max gets the same scrutiny as everything else, through search term visibility, asset group control, and brand exclusions.

Most accounts treat Google and Meta as two separate channels. One strategy, one report, and attribution that ties spend back to true blended CAC pulls them into a single system.

On the creative side, I build direct-response variations and test them against your current best performer, so budget follows what converts.

What happens after the click decides whether you get a customer. Landing pages, retargeting, and CRM automation in GoHighLevel keep the funnel from leaking, so every lead gets followed up before it goes cold.

Inherited a messy account? You get an audit and prioritized findings first, then a restructure, with the plan on the table before I touch the build. What usually turns up: campaigns bidding against each other, and a Performance Max campaign nobody has reviewed since launch.

For roofing, garage doors, HVAC and other home services, the conversion is a phone call and a booked job, not a form fill. Call tracking and tight geo-targeting come first, then the account gets measured on cost per booked job. For ecommerce and DTC brands I also run CRO on the 80/20, checkout and AOV.

Results
- 97% reduction in cost per lead for a home improvement contractor
- 13.24x ROAS and $619k in sales for a furniture DTC brand (Meta Ads)
- 7.66x ROAS and €268k in sales from zero in 90 days (gym equipment, Google Ads)
- ROAS from 249% to 466% in 3 months for a global beauty brand
- 77% more qualified leads and 32% lower CPA for a B2B SaaS company

What I Work With
Google Ads (Search, Shopping, Performance Max, Display, YouTube), Meta/Facebook Ads, Bing Ads. GA4, Google Tag Manager, Meta Pixel, server-side tracking (Stape). Google Merchant Center, Shopify. GoHighLevel, Zapier, Make, n8n. Day to day: keyword research, negative keywords, bid strategy, ad copy testing, A/B testing, retargeting, landing page optimization, and reporting.

"Since working with Kamil, average monthly sales increased from $4,000 to $25,600" - Peter S, Loft Design

Not a fit if you want someone who reports clicks and impressions, needs weeks before acting, or can't define a numeric kill rule. I'm measured on output.

If your ads aren't performing, or you can't tell because you don't trust the numbers, message me and I'll tell you the first thing I check.

["Want to AI enable your CRM without creating chaos?

The chaos is not caused by AI. It is caused by automating a process nobody wrote down.

✳️ What I actually do

○ Diagnosis. Current state mapping of systems, data and process. Where revenue leaks, what it costs, and in what order to fix it. You get the map whether or not you continue.

○ Platform architecture. HubSpot (Klavyo, GoHighLevel, PipeDrive, Intercom) implementation and migration across Marketing, Sales, Service and Operations Hub. Lifecycle and pipeline design that matches how you actually sell, not how the template assumes you sell.

○ Integration and data. Custom API work and operational systems, quote to cash and order flow, deduplication and data structuring.

- n8n, make, zapier, Clay
- QuickBooks, Stripe
- Central Dispatch, Guesty, EasyOTA, VacationCRM
- Slack, Hive, ClickUp, Asana
- Fireflies, AskElephant, Read.ai, Fathom

○ Process design and documentation. Every process is written down and handed over. This is the change management, not an afterthought to it.

○ Reporting and decision infrastructure. Attribution, forecasting, dashboards and the definitions underneath them, so that two people looking at the same number agree on what it means.

○ Enablement and people. Training an internal owner to run the system after I leave, and helping you hire that person if they are not already on the team.

○ AI enablement. Last, on top of a defined process, where it removes real hours rather than adding a new category of error.

✳️ The leaks, by stage

○ Pre revenue and pilots. Everything lives in the founder's head. Trials and site visits have no pipeline stage, so nobody can tell a real evaluation from a polite conversation. No data structure, which means your first commercial hire inherits nothing and starts from zero.

○ First reps, early go to market. Process was never defined, so each rep invents their own. Reporting cannot tell you which motion actually worked, only which rep is loudest. You cannot hold anyone accountable to a standard that does not exist in writing.

○ Scaling, roughly 3M to 30M. Tool sprawl. Two systems hold the same customer and disagree. Quoting happens in spreadsheets outside the CRM. Someone retypes the same information into five places every week. Attribution breaks precisely when you start spending real money on channels.

○ 30M and beyond. Multi entity, multi geo, direct and channel conflict. Handoffs between marketing, sales and service leak at the seams. Forecast integrity becomes a board-level problem rather than an inconvenience.

Tell me your stage and I can usually name three of your leaks before you show me the system. That is not intuition. It is pattern recognition across fifteen years of the same problems arriving in the same order.

✳️ How I work, in sequence

Select or audit your existing CRM, tool stack, and GTM. Then documented process. Then the right people in the right seats. Then automation and AI.

That order is not negotiable and it is the reason I get called in after other agencies. Automating an undefined process produces faster mistakes and a more expensive cleanup. Most firms sell the last step first because it is the easiest thing to sell.

○ I lead the transformation, I do not just recommend one. Vision through to technical execution. I am in the build.

For some it was segmentation architecture at scale of 2M contacts built spanning 16 sub industries across both B2B and B2C. For others it was ad management and spend accountability. In some cases it was sophisticated lead gen and AI sales automation.

I'll be your partner in sales and marketing consulting, fractional CMO, RevOps work building go to market strategy for companies at every stage of growth, optimizing your revenue and fueling your growth.

["Hi,

- Fixing implementations that stalled or never delivered what was promised
- Tightening up an existing org that has drifted out of sync with how the team actually works

I try to keep the work grounded in your sales motion, service workflow, and revenue goals rather than starting from the platform's defaults. In most cases, what looks like a CRM problem turns out to be a process problem the CRM is making louder.

Platforms I work with day to day:
- HubSpot CRM: Sales, Marketing, Service, Operations, and CMS Hubs
- Salesforce: Sales Cloud, Service Cloud, Marketing Cloud, Experience Cloud, Pardot, CPQ, Agentforce
- Microsoft Dynamics 365: Sales, Customer Service, Marketing, Field Service, Power Platform
- AWS: Connect, Lambda, EventBridge, S3, mostly for middleware and integrations

Where I typically add value:
- CRM selection and architecture, with honest tradeoff analysis
- End-to-end implementations and customizations
- Migrations between platforms with minimal disruption
- Agentforce architectures, including multi-agent topologies and custom Foundation Layers
- Integrations to ERP, finance, marketing, and support systems
- Process optimization across sales, service, and marketing
- CRM health checks with prioritized fix recommendations
- Training and adoption work for the teams that have to live with the system

- Helped a B2B SaaS team move off Salesforce to HubSpot. They saved roughly $60K a year in licensing and got noticeably better adoption from sales.
- Implemented Microsoft Dynamics 365 Sales for a global manufacturer. Forecast accuracy moved from around 58 percent to about 89 percent over two quarters.
- Ran a CRM selection for a Series B fintech and recommended HubSpot over Salesforce. The TCO model showed close to $200K saved across implementation and the first year of ops.
- Built an AWS-based integration hub connecting Dynamics 365, NetSuite, and a custom portal. The manual data reconciliation that used to consume about 30 hours a week dropped to a few minutes a day.
- Audited a Salesforce org for an insurance broker. We consolidated 12 legacy custom objects and brought storage costs down by nearly half.
- Led a CRM consolidation after an acquisition, merging HubSpot and Salesforce environments. Licensing dropped about $120K a year and reporting got a lot cleaner.

Industries I've worked in:
SaaS, manufacturing, financial services, healthcare, professional services, e-commerce, real estate, education, and insurance.

What it's like to work with me:
I try to be useful rather than busy. That usually means suggesting the smaller fix before the bigger project, pushing back when a feature request doesn't match the underlying goal, and staying relatively quiet on the parts of the platform that are working fine. Updates come weekly, with a Loom walkthrough when something is easier to show than to write. I overlap with US, EU, and APAC working hours.

Send me a message about your project. I reply within a few hours and we can take it from there.

description:
["Your Figma file is ready to build, or I fix it free. That's the Build-Ready Guarantee.

Most SaaS design doesn't fail in Figma. It fails at handoff. The screens look right, your developers start building, and then the questions start: what happens in the empty state, what does this table do at 10,000 rows, which of these three modals is the real one. Half the sprint goes into decisions that should have been made in design — and you pay twice, once for the design and once for the rework.

I'm a product designer for SaaS, AI and data-heavy B2B platforms: dashboards, analytics, fintech, HR, learning platforms, internal tools with several user roles.

THE BUILD-READY GUARANTEE
A missing screen, state or edge case inside the agreed scope, and I fix it free. I can offer that because every file passes a dedicated design QA reviewer before it reaches your developers — a separate person whose only job is to reject my work before your engineers have to. Most design studios don't have this role at all.

HOW I WORK
- Discovery first: 10+ user interviews per role and 30+ quantitative responses before anything gets designed. If the research says the product isn't ready, I say so.
- Scope discipline: a typical intake goes from 40 requested features to the dozen that actually carry the product. Cutting is most of the value.
- Design for the users we identified, not for taste: every screen answers a documented user, job and barrier.
- Dev-ready output: flows, states, edge cases, empty and error states, tokens and specs your engineers can build from — or your AI agent can build from.

WHAT I CAN START WITH
1. Discovery & UX Research Sprint — $2,500, 2 weeks. Research, PRD, scoping, information architecture and the first 3 design concepts. This is the sprint that makes everything after it buildable — by a dev team or by an AI agent.
2. Product Teardown — $1,500, 1 week. A UX audit of your existing product: named friction points, severity, and what each one costs you.
3. AI-Ready Build Spec — from $3,000. PRD, product architecture and interface spec structured so an AI build agent produces something coherent instead of 40 screens of guesswork.
4. Landing Page Design — from $1,500.
5. Website Design — from $5,000.
6. Product Design — from $8,000. Full product UX/UI plus the design system, dev-ready.

NUMBERS I CAN ACTUALLY SHOW YOU
- 100% Job Success, 47 jobs, 3,831 hours tracked here
- 23 product engagements delivered, clients in the US, EU and UK
- A PPC click-fraud platform: 20% more users completing signup after the redesign
- A marketing-led SaaS: from 1,000 to 10,000 users after the website rebuild
- A trading platform from zero: 40 requested features scoped down to the 12 that shipped

I won't quote you a conversion percentage I can't source. I'll name the barrier and the mechanism instead — the same way I'd do it on your product.

WHO'S BEHIND ME
I run design at Basa Solutions, a 14-person studio: 10 designers, 2 PMs, a tech lead and the design QA reviewer above. You work with me. When a project needs a second designer, build support or QA capacity, it's already there and you don't restart the hiring.

Not a fit if you need a logo, a pitch deck, or screens approved by taste alone.

Send me your product and where it's stuck, or book the 30-minute consultation and I'll give you the first read before either of us commits to anything.Show less"]

I've spent the last 7 years designing and shipping AI-native products from end to end. First frame in Figma to deployed React or Next.js app. Web and mobile. Here's what that actually looks like:
Product and UX design. I run discovery, map user flows, sketch wireframes, build high-fidelity UI, and wire up interactive prototypes in Figma and Framer. What you get isn't a static file. It's a prototype your engineers can actually build against.

Design systems:
Tokenized component libraries in Figma, with matching code in Tailwind, shadcn/ui, or a custom setup for your stack. Built to grow, documented so your team can keep extending it after I'm gone.

Frontend and full-stack development:
-On the web: React, Next.js 14 and 15, TypeScript, Tailwind, Framer Motion, GSAP.
-On mobile: React Native and Expo, shipping to iOS and Android from one codebase.
When the backend needs to be mine too: Node.js, FastAPI, Postgres.

AI product work:
Chat interfaces, voice UIs, RAG-powered search, agent workflows, structured LLM outputs. I've shipped this kind of work across healthcare, hiring, real estate, and property management.

My 2026 AI toolkit:
Claude Code and Codex for shipping frontend at a genuinely different pace. Figma Make and Framer for design-to-code. Cursor, v0, Bolt, and Lovable when the goal is fast prototypes. Figma MCP for automating large design files. If your team is used to slow, cautious design-then-build cycles, working with me will feel like changing gears.

A quick tour of recent work:
-A full multi-page marketing site for an AI hiring product. Audience-specific pages for candidates, recruiters, interviewers, and HR leaders. Hero video, complex interactions, everything designed and coded by me with no handoff friction.

-AI leasing assistant and voice-AI demo interfaces for a property management startup. iOS-style phone mockups, exported as pixel-perfect demo video for GTM use.

-Healthcare revenue-integrity dashboards. Audit logs, claim workflows, dense data views that stay readable instead of overwhelming.

-React Native and Next.js SaaS builds, with matching design systems in Figma so design and code stay in sync.

-Design system audits and Figma-to-code handoffs across 20+ SaaS products.

Where I do my best work:
SaaS and enterprise dashboards. Healthcare and revenue integrity. Fintech and payments. Property management and real estate. Hiring and HR tech. IoT and consumer hardware. On-demand mobile apps.

Tech I actually ship with:
-Design: Figma, Framer, Figma Make, Figma MCP, prototyping, design tokens.
-Web frontend: React, Next.js, TypeScript, Tailwind, shadcn/ui, Framer Motion, GSAP.
-Mobile: React Native, Swift, Kotlin, Flutter, native iOS and Android UI patterns.
-Backend when needed: Node.js, FastAPI, Postgres, Firebase, Supabase, Python
-AI stack: OpenAI, Anthropic Claude, RAG (pgvector), voice AI, agent patterns.
-AI-native tooling: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, v0, Bolt, Lovable.
-Deploy: Vercel, Netlify, Cloudflare, Custom Domain

What it's like to work with me:
I ask a lot of questions in week one. After that, I share progress often, in whatever tool your team already lives in: Linear, Notion, Slack, Jira, or Figma comments. If I think an idea won't work, I say so and I explain why. If I make a mistake, I own it and I fix it fast.

I care about outcomes more than tickets:
On a typical engagement, I research the problem, design the solution, prototype it, and ship the frontend. Usually in that order. Sometimes all at once. I write my own UX copy, handle the deploy, and iterate live with your team instead of waiting for weekly reviews.

Who tends to hire me:
Startup founders who need one person to take an AI idea from zero to a working product. Product leads at scaleups who want a senior hand on a complex feature. Agencies looking for a specialist to plug into a client build. Enterprise teams that want a designer who can also ship the code.

If any of that fits, send me a message. Tell me what you're building, where you're stuck, and what "done" looks like for you. I'll reply within a day with an honest read on whether I'm the right fit, plus a rough sense of timeline and cost.

Looking forward to hearing what you're working on.Show less']

description:
["SOURCE-CRITICAL HISTORICAL RESEARCH & EDITING

I help authors, filmmakers, publishers, archaeologists, heritage professionals, museums, and research teams turn complex historical and cultural evidence into clear, accurate, publication-ready work.

I am a PhD historian, research consultant, and editor with 15+ years of experience in historical research, university teaching, source criticism, fact-checking, scholarly review, developmental editing, and research-based writing. I have worked as an Associate Professor of History and as a history subject-matter expert, editor, and reviewer for the Ministry of Education and Science of Georgia.

My work is especially suited to projects where sources conflict, evidence is incomplete, traditions have accumulated over time, or claims require careful verification before publication or production.

CORE EXPERTISE

My research areas include Georgia and the Caucasus, Byzantium and the Black Sea world, medieval history, historical geography and cartography, mythology and folklore, cultural history and ethnography, genealogy and heraldry, archaeology and heritage, fortifications and sacred landscapes, political and intellectual history, imperial narratives, and the history of medicine and medical ideas.

PRIMARY SOURCES & MANUSCRIPTS

I work with primary sources, manuscripts, archival materials, and historical objects. My specialist research includes textual criticism, prosopography, codicology, manuscript transmission, numismatics, epigraphy, paleography, historical heraldry, toponymy, and onomastics.

I can read medieval Georgian manuscripts in Asomtavruli and Nuskhuri scripts and work with textual variants, colophons, dating, provenance, scribal features, and transmission history. I also have university training in Ancient Greek and Latin.

My object-based research includes the analysis of coins, inscriptions, seals, heraldry, maps, and historical photographs in relation to chronology, identity, authority, provenance, and historical context.

EDITORIAL & MANUSCRIPT WORK

I provide developmental editing, copy editing, proofreading, editorial writing, and source-critical review for historical, academic, cultural, and research-based content.

I assess argument, structure, chronology, narrative flow, evidentiary balance, repetition, audience suitability, and the relationship between claims and sources. I identify gaps, inconsistencies, unsupported conclusions, and areas requiring clarification, restructuring, or further research.

I also improve clarity, accuracy, consistency, terminology, tone, transitions, citations, captions, bibliographies, and readability while preserving the author's voice.

SERVICES

• Historical research dossiers & source evaluation
• Fact-checking & claim verification
• Developmental editing & manuscript assessment
• Copy editing, proofreading & editorial review
• Historical accuracy & source-critical review
• Archival, genealogical & prosopographical research
• Mythology, folklore & cultural-history research
• Heraldic, epigraphic, numismatic & manuscript research
• Historical geography, cartography, archaeology & heritage research
• Research for books, documentaries, screenplays, exhibitions & games
• Chronologies, annotated bibliographies & literature reviews

RESEARCH METHOD

I distinguish between directly attested evidence, strong scholarly inference, plausible reconstruction, later tradition or interpretation, and unsupported speculation.

I trace claims to their sources, compare conflicting accounts, identify chronological and interpretive problems, explain the limits of surviving evidence, and recommend the strongest wording the evidence can responsibly support.

LANGUAGES & COMMUNICATION

Georgian is my native language. I work with English-language materials and sources in German and Russian. My historical-language training includes Ancient Greek and Latin.

For research and editorial projects, I work primarily through written communication so that sources, decisions, citations, and revisions remain documented. Calls can be arranged when useful.

Send me your manuscript, research question, period or region, intended format, available sources, and deadline. I can recommend an appropriate research or editorial scope, methodology, and deliverable.Show less"]

description:
["I help local service businesses stop guessing which ads bring jobs. I connect CallRail, GoHighLevel and GA4 to trace every call and form to the ad that paid for it, so you spend where jobs come from.

Right now you can probably tell me what you spend on ads and roughly how many calls came in last month. But can you tell me which of those calls turned into booked jobs?

If your channels share one number, your team forgets to tag the source, and leads go cold in GoHighLevel after one text, you're cutting ad budget blind.

Now picture this. Every channel has its own CallRail tracking number. The source lands on the GoHighLevel contact by itself. Missed calls get a text back in seconds, and your GHL follow up keeps going until the lead replies or books. That's what I build.

Ad, Google LSA or website visit ➜ CallRail tracking number or GoHighLevel form ➜ source saved on the GHL contact ➜ pipeline moves to Booked ➜ conversion sent back to Google Ads and Meta ➜ cost per booked job on your dashboard

Hi, I'm Joel. GoHighLevel Expert, HighLevel Certified Admin and Top Rated on Upwork, with 141 jobs, 767 hours and a 94% Job Success Score. I've worked in GoHighLevel (GHL) for four years, alongside CallRail, GA4, Google Tag Manager, HubSpot, Pipedrive, Zapier, Make and Twilio.

🏆 Some of the businesses I've helped
1. LJ Hooker Property Collective, real estate. An eleven phase GoHighLevel lead nurture system with seller and buyer pipelines and lead scoring.
2. A home service business. CallRail call tracking setup so every call traced back to its source.
3. Templaris. A GoHighLevel marketing strategy build.
4. Rhodes Alliance. Full GoHighLevel setup over two months, funnel, CRM and workflow automation.
5. Optinize GmbH, a sales agency. Pipedrive CRM implementation.
6. MAKAI GROUP. Mindbody data sent to Google Sheets automatically through Zapier.
7. The Work Shop. Emailed leads pushed into Pipedrive through Zapier.
8. CliniContact. Twilio and Monday connected for their practice managers.
9. A reputation management company. GoHighLevel automations for their reputation dashboard.
10. Investlogic Group, property. An email nurture sequence built into their CRM.

What I take off your plate
📞 Call tracking in CallRail. A tracking number per channel and dynamic number insertion on your website
🎯 Lead attribution. UTMs and GCLID captured on GoHighLevel forms, lead source carried onto the contact and through the pipeline
📈 Conversion tracking. GA4, Google Tag Manager, Google Ads offline conversions and Meta Conversions API, so your ads learn from booked jobs, not clicks
⚙️ GoHighLevel CRM setup. GHL pipelines, sub-accounts, custom fields and calendars with routing
🔁 GoHighLevel automation. GHL workflows, missed call text back, lead nurture and follow up that keeps going until someone replies
🧲 GoHighLevel funnels. Landing pages, forms and appointment booking funnels
⭐ Review requests and database reactivation of old leads
✅ A2P 10DLC registration through to approval
🧩 GHL snapshots agencies can clone across every client sub-account

How I work
Audit ➜ fix plan ➜ build ➜ test with real calls and forms ➜ handover with a dashboard, SOP and Loom

Ways to work with me
🔍 Attribution audit. Where your leads come from, what's broken and the order to fix it.
🛠️ Lead system build. GoHighLevel plus the CallRail and GA4 tracking layer, handed over with a dashboard and a simple SOP.
📦 Agency snapshot. The same GHL build made to clone, with docs and a Loom walkthrough.
📅 Monthly GoHighLevel support. Monitoring, reports and changes as your campaigns move.

💡 Worth knowing: a phone system routes calls, it doesn't carry the source. If tracking sits behind it, every call shows up as direct. That one mistake is why most lead dashboards can't be trusted.

FAQs
Do I have to switch CRMs?
No. If you're on GoHighLevel I build inside it. If you're on HubSpot or Pipedrive, the source still lands on the contact there.

Will my main phone number change?
No. Your main number stays. CallRail tracking numbers forward to it.

How long does it take?
An audit takes 2 to 3 days. A full GoHighLevel and call tracking build is usually 1 to 2 weeks after I get access.

Send me a message and answer one question. Does every channel have its own number, or are they all sharing one? I'll tell you what I'd fix first before you pay anything.Show less"]

title_occupation: ['QA Tester | QA Engineer | QA Automation | Software Testing']
description:
["🚀 Transforming QA from a Bottleneck into a Business Advantage

As a detail-oriented QA Engineer, I help B2B SaaS, complex fintech platforms, and fast-moving mobile startups accelerate their delivery cycles without ever sacrificing quality. By taking absolute end-to-end ownership of the testing process, I minimize post-release business risks, prevent revenue-impacting bugs, and ensure your software ships quickly as a stable, production-ready product.

I understand that in Agile environments, speed is just as important as stability. My goal is to catch critical issues before they reach your customers, protecting your brand reputation and saving development time.


🔍 Comprehensive Quality Assurance: Manual & Automated

With over 5,000 hours of Software Testing experience across 30+ platforms, I operate effectively as both a meticulous manual QA Tester and a highly technical QA Automation specialist. I don’t just check if a feature works on the sunny-day paths; I simulate complex user flows, dig into unintuitive areas, and rigorously validate edge cases to ensure your system doesn't break under real-world pressure.

Whether I’m stepping in as an exploratory Tester or a strategic Automation Engineer, my approach guarantees a high-quality bar. I bridge the gap between user expectations and technical execution, providing a safety net for your engineering team.

My Core Testing Methodologies:

🧪 Functional & Exploratory Testing: Navigating the app like a real user to uncover non-obvious logical errors and UX friction points.

🔄 Thorough Regression Testing: Ensuring that new code merges never break existing, legacy functionality. Every Test phase I run is structured and methodical.

⚙️ API Validation: Going beyond the UI. I inspect network requests, validate JSON responses, and ensure flawless backend-to-frontend data integrity using tools like Postman and Chrome DevTools.

📱 Mobile Device Testing: Validating responsive design, cross-platform UI consistency, network interruptions, and memory scenarios on actual iOS and Android devices.


🛠️ Technical Stack & Frameworks

To provide maximum test coverage and efficiency, I build custom solutions and adapt quickly to your existing CI/CD pipelines.

UI & E2E Automation: I write robust custom scripts in Python and JavaScript (using Selenium WebDriver, Pytest) and am highly adaptable to modern testing frameworks like Cypress and Playwright.

Performance & Load: Using tools like Locust to stress-test your system, identify memory leaks, and verify infrastructure health under high concurrent loads.

API Testing: Advanced Postman collections, REST/GraphQL validation, and deep log inspection.

Management & Tracking: Mastery of Jira, Confluence, TestRail, and Hiptest for maintaining comprehensive test documentation.


📊 Proven Track Record & Project Ownership

I've led QA teams of 4–8 specialists and managed the full quality lifecycle for highly demanding applications, from MVPs to high-load enterprise platforms:

☁️ SaaS & Enterprise B2B: Acted as the lead QA and Automation Tester, building automated pipelines from the ground up. I verified complex business logic, role-based access controls, and data processing for logistics platforms and real estate CRMs.

📈 Fintech & Trading: Handled full-cycle quality assurance for a high-stakes trading platform. I designed and executed complex test scenarios where accuracy and system reliability were non-negotiable.

📱 Native & Cross-Platform Mobile: Executed deep mobile app testing across iOS (Swift/TestFlight) and Android. I handled everything from API integrations and rapid user interactions to validating core posting flows and location-based features.

🏥 Compliance & Healthcare: Performed detailed API and performance testing in a regulated environment where precision and clear documentation are mandatory.


🤝 Seamless Workflow & Clear Communication

I'm a strong believer that QA is a communication role as much as a technical one. I don't just wait for instructions — I act proactively.

📝 Actionable Bug Reports: I log defects directly in Jira with absolute clarity. My reports always include expected vs. actual results, severity ratings (Critical, Major, Minor), environment details, and exact, reproducible steps so your dev team doesn't have to guess or ask follow-up questions.

🗣️ Clear Communication: I collaborate closely with developers, product managers, and designers using clear written English to resolve ambiguities early in the sprint.

⚙️ Continuous Integration: I integrate a continuous feedback loop directly into your agile workflow to ensure stable mobile and web releases.


If you're looking for a proactive professional who can hit the ground running, take ownership of your quality standards, and deliver bulletproof results, I'm ready to join your team. Let's connect and build something exceptional together!Show less"]

Whether you're launching a new business or refreshing an existing one, I can help create a visual identity that reflects your vision and connects with your audience.

Already have a logo that needs to be recreated?

description:
["Say you only have one reason why anyone should
ever buy your product, and maybe it stopped working since March.
So, now you're basically paying copywriters to pump out new adjectives.

Or maybe you've even reshot that winning ad six times now. New hook, new clip, a different creator once, but the same idea underneath every single time.

Look (and I hate to say this), a new hook on a dead angle is just lipstick on a corpse.

And let’s be clear, not one of those writers actually did anything wrong. You asked for ads and they simply wrote more ads. I mean, none of them was getting paid to walk in and tell you the 'real' problem.
I've been on that side too. You don't say it. You just take the money and you write the ninth version of the same angle and hope one of them catches.

But you know what?

Ten ads made from one idea isn't creative testing. It's just one test you ran ten times, and you already paid for the same outcome nine times over.

Now, here's what took me way too long to learn: ads actually die THREE ways and almost everyone treats them the same.

Hooks die in days, and that's quite cheap. Reshoot it, change the first three seconds, and you're fine.
The reason dies in weeks, so you keep the argument and just build a new format for it.
But the angle underneath (I mean the actual why-anyone-should-buy-this), that one dies in months.
And when it goes, nothing you ever shoot brings it back. You can spend forty grand finding that out. Most people do actually, because when a hook dies it looks identical to when a reason dies, and if you can't tell them apart you'll keep buying variations while the thing that's actually broken sits there untouched.

So that's the first thing I do: diagnose what stopped working, what it used to do, and which of the three actually died. Then I write.

Four years of this now, mostly in supplements, caffeine, sneakers, skincare and sleep niche. Pretty much things people buy on impulse and justify afterward.
There's a psych degree behind me somewhere too, which matters much less than those four years but probably explains why I go digging for the reason before I go looking for words.

What I actually write: Meta and TikTok ads. Hooks, statics, scripts. UGC that doesn't sound scripted. YouTube ads people actually finish. Brand voice, if yours currently reads like a policy document. Cold email, when it needs to get a reply from someone who owes you absolutely nothing.

Two kinds of people should AVOID me:

Anyone who wants safe. Safe copy only reads great in meetings but dies online really quickly, and I'm bad at pretending otherwise.
And anyone who wants ten more of what's already dying, because I'll tell you it's dying, you'll be irritated, and we'll both lose a week finding out we were never going to get along.

Otherwise: send me the ad that stopped working and roughly what it used to do. Two days, no charge, and you'll get back what actually killed it (hook, idea, or reason) plus two other reasons people buy your product that you're not using yet.

Read them. And if none of them is news, don't reply. I'll take the hint.
Show less"]

description:
['I design and build automation systems centered on n8n, Make, Openclaw, Claude-Code, UiPath, and Zapier to remove repetitive work and connect the tools your team already uses. I create workflows that use webhooks and API calls to fetch data, trigger jobs and move information between Airtable, Google Sheets, Gmail and CRMs. I run scraping and data collection inside no code workflows when it makes sense and I combine those flows with external services for parsing, proxy rotation and scheduling. My focus is on clear maintainable flows that are easy to operate and hand over.

Clients often ask for reliable workflow automation, API integration, webhooks, data extraction and production ready systems that handle rate limits and retries. I build automations that include notification steps to Gmail and Slack, automatic updates to Airtable and Google Drive and webhooks to trigger Python services when logic gets complex. I design each workflow so it is auditable with logs and failure handling and I document how secrets, API keys and credentials are stored and rotated. I follow patterns seen in many client requests for workflow reliability and clear documentation.

Python data scraping and extraction
I use Python to build reliable data scraping and extraction systems when projects need custom logic or large scale collection. I work with Scrapy, BeautifulSoup, Selenium and requests to handle pagination, retries, session cookies, proxies and anti blocking measures. I use pandas for data cleaning, transformation and validation, including date normalization and merging multiple datasets. The final data can be delivered in CSV, JSON, SQL databases or synced directly to Airtable and Google Sheets.

Python web development and APIs
For backend services and automation interfaces, I build APIs using FastAPI, Django REST framework and Flask. These APIs provide stable and well documented endpoints that can be called from n8n, webhooks or other systems. I containerize applications using Docker and prepare deployment setups for cloud platforms such as AWS, Heroku and managed container services. This allows automations and scraping systems to run reliably in production environments.

How I work
I start by clarifying the exact outcome you want and the systems where data must land. I map the workflow end to end and I choose whether each task should run inside n8n or inside a Python service. I provide a simple diagram and a short plan so you can approve before development starts. I build with retries, idempotency and test data so the automation can recover from common errors. I add monitoring and alerts so you know when a workflow fails and why. I also prepare a handover plan that explains how to run, monitor and update the automation after delivery, following best practices for clear client handoff.

Deliverables and integrations
You will receive the n8n workflow files, Python code with clear instructions and an operations guide that explains how to run, edit and troubleshoot the system. I integrate with Airtable using the Airtable API for structured data, with Gmail for notifications and with Google Sheets or databases for reporting. I can connect CRMs, payment systems and chat apps on request so the automation becomes part of your business processes. The Airtable API follows REST semantics and makes it straightforward to sync and link records between systems.

AI and smart enrichment
I add AI agents and GPT based enrichment where it helps, for example classifying content, extracting entities, summarizing pages and creating human friendly descriptions. AI steps run either via API calls inside n8n or inside Python services that call OpenAI or other models. This reduces manual review and saves hours by turning raw scraped text into structured tagged data ready for analytics and reporting. I can also build agent flows that decide whether a record needs manual review or can be pushed to storage or to an analyst for final checks.

Quality security and handover
I write tests for critical parts, document expected inputs and outputs and store credentials securely. I follow common security practices for API keys and tokens and I add rate limiting and proxy support for scraping jobs. I add logging so you can trace failures and I include health checks and alerts to Slack or email. I hand over the workflows, the code and an operations checklist so your team can run and extend the automations. I also offer short training sessions and free minor fixes during the first two weeks after delivery.

If you want a reliable automation that uses n8n together with Python for custom tasks, Airtable and Gmail integrations and optional AI enrichment, send me a brief and I will reply with a clear plan, an estimate and sample workflow ideas. description:
["I run self-hosted Odoo in production, including one instance that bills around 4,300 consumers end to end. None of it is ever touched over SSH, including by me, because every change goes through a pipeline that rolls the database and the code back together when a deploy fails its own check.

Running Odoo on your own servers and something needs to move, break less, or get upgraded? Send me your version, your module list and how you deploy today. I'll send back a short recorded review of what I'd fix first and what's already fine. Free, inside 48 hours, no obligation, and no pitch at the end of it.

Most Odoo developers can build modules but can't run the infrastructure underneath them. Most DevOps engineers have never opened an Odoo manifest. The work I do sits in the middle, which is where self-hosted Odoo projects usually break. I'm CTO at ONPOINT XS, an Odoo Partner, and it's the same work there as here.

WHAT I RUN IN PRODUCTION

A corporate ERP on Odoo 19 Enterprise covering HR, payroll, finance, procurement, attendance and document management. Live since July 2026. Its document store sits on S3-compatible object storage. Production is operated entirely through GitHub Actions on a self-hosted runner. Nobody SSHes into that server, including me.

A utility billing system on Odoo 18 Community for a housing authority, billing roughly 4,300 consumers end to end. Metering, tariff engine, formula-driven bill calculation, net metering with credit carry-forward, collections, QWeb bill templates, and a REST API feeding an Android field app for meter readings.

Across both systems the issue register stands at 261 closed of 308.

SELF-HOSTED AI, THE SAME DISCIPLINE

More of this work now means running models on your own hardware instead of sending your data to somebody's API. GPU provisioning, Ollama and inference servers in Docker, retrieval plumbing, and the parts nobody plans for: VRAM headroom once requests arrive concurrently, a driver or CUDA version drifting out of step with the container, and what happens when the box reboots mid-inference.

Same Linux, same Docker, same backups, same rollback discipline as the ERP work. To be clear about the boundary: I have fine-tuned an open-weight language model and adapted a speech model for domain audio on a production project, and I can do that again. What I don't do is model research or novel architectures. If you need somebody to invent the approach, that's a data scientist. If you need it fine-tuned, served and kept running on hardware you control, that's me.

HOW I DEPLOY

- Docker Compose, with staging and production kept properly separate
- Every pull request gated on lint and the full Odoo test suite. It blocks the merge.
- Images pinned by digest, so an upstream tag change can't quietly alter your build
- Dependency-ordered module upgrades with a post-deploy assertion that checks the version actually moved. If it didn't, the pipeline rolls back the database and the code instead of reporting success.
- Restic backups every six hours, restore-drilled, with the encryption key held by the customer

WHAT I WORK ON

- Odoo version upgrades with full data migration
- Self-hosted deployment on AWS, Hetzner, or your own hardware
- Migrating off Odoo.sh or Odoo Online onto infrastructure you control
- Multi-tenant and multi-database setups
- Odoo REST APIs and third-party integrations
- CI/CD pipelines for Odoo
- PostgreSQL and performance tuning
- Self-hosted LLM and GPU infrastructure
- Rescuing self-hosted instances nobody can safely upgrade any more

HOW I WORK

I start with your current version, module list, and what's actually customised, because that determines whether an upgrade is a weekend or a month. Most quotes get this wrong.

Then you get a written plan with the risks named up front. I write documentation and runbooks so your team can operate the system after I'm gone.

description:
["Need a WordPress Developer who can also fix the performance problems slowing your site down?

Slow WordPress site? Poor Core Web Vitals? Elementor or WooCommerce getting heavier every month? You don't need another plugin thrown at the problem. You need to know what is actually slowing the site down, and what's worth fixing.

I diagnose the underlying problem, then fix it at the WordPress, theme, plugin, database, CSS/JS, image, server, caching, or third-party script level. The goal isn't just a higher PageSpeed Insights or GTmetrix score. It's a faster, more stable, easier-to-maintain website that performs better for real users on mobile and desktop, and passes Core Web Vitals in Google Search Console.

HOW I SOLVE IT:

Every project starts with a technical site speed audit and a performance baseline using PageSpeed Insights, GTmetrix, and Search Console field data (LCP, INP, CLS). I identify the real bottlenecks instead of guessing, prioritize the fixes that actually move the needle, implement them cleanly without breaking your design or functionality, then test the result across mobile and desktop.

You get a clear before-and-after report so you can verify the improvement yourself, not just take my word for it.

I CAN HELP WITH:

- WordPress development and customization
- WordPress & WooCommerce development and performance optimization
- Page Speed Optimization using PageSpeed Insights and GTmetrix
- Core Web Vitals: LCP, INP, CLS (lab data and real-user field data)
- Elementor, Kadence, GeneratePress, Astra and Divi
- Custom PHP, JavaScript, HTML and CSS
- Technical SEO and site speed audits
- Crawl, index, sitemap and schema markup issues
- Cloudflare, LiteSpeed, Nginx and Apache
- WP Rocket, LiteSpeed Cache and Perfmatters
- Database, image, CSS and JavaScript optimization
- Mobile optimization and mobile performance
- CDN setup and configuration
- WordPress migrations, cloning, staging and backups
- Google Search Console setup and error resolution
- Third-party script and integration performance issues
- WordPress troubleshooting and ongoing maintenance
- Website security hardening and malware cleanup

TYPICAL PROBLEMS I FIX:

1. Homepage or product pages failing LCP because of unoptimized hero images or slow server response
2. Layout shift (CLS) from ads, fonts, or images loading without dimensions set
3. Slow interactivity (INP) from heavy, render-blocking JavaScript and bloated page builders
4. WooCommerce stores slowing down as products, plugins, and orders pile up
5. Sites that score well in PageSpeed but still fail Core Web Vitals in Search Console, because lab data and real-user field data are not the same thing
6. Migrations from one theme or builder to another without losing rankings or breaking layouts
7. High-traffic sites becoming unstable under load, with intermittent errors or timeouts

WHY ME:

Since 2019, I've worked on 830+ WordPress and WooCommerce sites, helping businesses fix performance problems, pass Core Web Vitals, clean up bloated builds, and maintain faster, more stable websites long-term.

My advantage is the combination of WordPress development plus performance optimization in one person. Most speed specialists can only recommend changes. I can work on the implementation directly, in the theme, the plugins, the database, and the server config, instead of handing you a generic report and walking away.

I run ProSpeedGuy, where I lead a small team of developers, designers, and SEO specialists for larger projects, but every audit and every performance fix I deliver personally is hands-on, not outsourced.

MY APPROACH:

* Diagnose before changing
* Fix causes, not symptoms
* Avoid unnecessary plugins and complexity
* Measure before and after with real data
* Build for mobile first
* Focus on long-term maintainability
* Re-audit if an agreed performance target isn't met

Whether your site is on shared hosting, a managed WordPress host like WP Engine, Cloudways, or SiteGround, or a high-traffic WooCommerce store, I adjust the approach to what your setup can actually support, and I'll tell you upfront if hosting itself is the real limitation before any work starts.

['Most Klaviyo accounts don't have an email marketing problem. They have a flow that quietly stopped firing, and nobody noticed, because nothing looks broken.

The dashboard still loads. Campaigns still send. Revenue just sits lower than it should, and no one can say why.

Top Rated on Upwork. 92% Job Success Score, 40 completed jobs, 20 client reviews. Klaviyo Deliverability and Klaviyo Product certified, plus five HubSpot certifications.

That's the work I do. I take ownership of the retention channel for DTC ecommerce brands on Shopify and Shopify Plus: Klaviyo audits, flow architecture, campaign calendars, segmentation, deliverability, and full email design built in Figma through to live, editable templates. Health, beauty and wellness, supplements, skincare, wellness and beauty devices, grooming and intimate care, plus fashion, fragrance and home.

WHY FLOWS COME FIRST

Klaviyo's 2026 benchmark data, from more than 183,000 brands, shows flows produce close to 41% of total email revenue from just 5.3% of sends. The same pattern shows up inside accounts. On one European skincare brand, flows produced 90% of attributed email revenue, EUR 33,571 of EUR 37,188 in a 30-day window, up 106% month over month, while Klaviyo's own benchmarking rated the campaign side "Poor". A wellness device brand went from $0.00 to $3,288.66 in its first full month post-launch. A beauty device brand did $35,858 across a full BFCM and holiday season. All three are Klaviyo in-platform attribution rather than independently cross-checked store revenue, and I will always tell you which one you are looking at.

CORE FLOWS I BUILD AND OPTIMIZE

Welcome series, browse abandonment, cart abandonment, checkout abandonment, post-purchase, replenishment, cross-sell, winback and re-engagement, VIP, sunset. Triggers, conditional splits, timing, exclusions, suppression logic and profile properties set correctly, then tested live before launch. Abandoned cart should fire on Checkout Started, not Added to Cart, and the wrong trigger makes a working flow look weak.

WHAT I FIND IN AN AUDIT

A Shopify to Klaviyo integration needing a full reinstall before the abandoned cart trigger would fire at all. Roughly 5,000 profiles sitting outside every list and segment, caught before a Black Friday send. SPF, DKIM and DMARC misconfiguration traced from one test send landing in spam. A conversion metric tracking $0 revenue. None of these show up as errors. They show up as revenue that never arrives.

WHAT YOU GET

Audits: flow-by-flow diagnosis, deliverability check, list and segment health, integration verification, and written findings ranked by revenue impact.

Deliverability: domain authentication, sender reputation, list hygiene, suppression rules, sunset policy and re-warming. Health and wellness senders get filtered harder than any other sector.

Design and build: full design in Figma through to live, on-brand, editable Klaviyo templates, mobile and dark-mode tested, built to your brand guidelines. Design and implementation stay with one person. No designer-to-developer handoff.

Campaigns and segmentation: calendar planning, behavioural and lifecycle segments, A/B testing, popup and signup forms for list growth, and reporting that separates flow revenue from campaign revenue.

Migrations: platform moves with list, template and automation continuity intact, plus Shopify and CRM integration verified.

WHO I WORK BEST WITH

DTC brands on Shopify with a list that isn't earning what it should. Founders who have had email "set up" already and suspect it isn't working. Brands facing inbox placement problems. Agencies needing an individual freelance Klaviyo specialist who can diagnose, not just execute.

WHAT I DON'T DO

Cold outreach, purchased lists or bulk sending. Brand identity or logo work. And I don't take accounts where I can't get proper Klaviyo access, because diagnosis needs admin, not read-only.

NEXT STEP

Send me your Klaviyo account and what you think is wrong. I'll tell you what I'd check first, before any contract.

['Most AI projects fail before a line of code is written. Not because the technology is wrong, because the process underneath it is broken. Automating a broken process does not fix it. It just makes your team do the wrong thing faster.

We built Xandec around one principle: understand the problem first, fix the process second, build what is actually worth building. In that order. Always.

Who is behind Xandec:
I am Khizer, a Full-Stack AI Engineer and the founder of Xandec. I started my career building production software from the ground up, shipped across mobile, web, and AI systems simultaneously, and spent the last year embedded inside a US-based real estate and financial services company as their sole AI engineer, owning the entire technical layer, working directly with leadership, and transforming manual operations into automated intelligent systems. That engagement taught me something most developers never learn: the technology is rarely the hardest part. Understanding the business deeply enough to build the right thing is.

Xandec is the agency I built around that insight. A small, focused team that thinks like operators and builds like engineers. We take on a limited number of projects at a time so every client gets our full attention and direct access to the people actually building their system,not an account manager relaying messages to a team they have never met.

Three Things We Do. All Three Done Right.
1. Full-Stack SaaS Products, Zero to Production
You have an idea. We build it. Web apps, mobile apps, internal tools, client portals , shipped in four to eight weeks with clean architecture, real users, and production-grade code from day one. Not a prototype that needs a rebuild in six months. A system built to last and maintained after launch.
Industries we have shipped production SaaS in: fintech, healthcare, edtech, legal compliance, property management, and construction.

2. AI Deployment Across Your Organization: The FDE Model
This is not one chatbot for one team. This is the AI layer across your entire operation.
I lead every engagement personally. My job is to sit inside your operation, understand how each function actually works versus how it is supposed to work, fix the process before any automation begins, and then deploy a Forward Deployed Engineer to build the right thing. The FDE works function by function through your workflows, building and optimizing each process in sequence while I ensure the quality, business logic, and coherence of everything shipped.

We deployed this model at a US-based real estate and financial services company managing 800+ properties across three business divisions. Eight production automations connecting four separate business systems. Leasing pipeline automation eliminating manual data transfer. Compliance tracking across 800+ units surfacing deadline risks automatically. Construction bill payment automation removing 10+ hours of weekly double-entry. Mortgage pricing automation replacing a multi-day manual process with same-session delivery. Every system still running in production today.

The principle we never compromise: we will not automate your operation until we understand it. If your current process is broken we will tell you before we build anything. If a simpler non-AI solution solves the problem better we will recommend it.

3. Mobile and On-Device AI: Computer Vision and Real-Time Inference
Cross-platform iOS and Android applications with AI models running directly on the device. No cloud dependency, no latency, no API cost per inference. Computer vision, real-time object detection, movement analysis, and custom YOLO models running at 30+ FPS on mid-range hardware.
We have shipped production applications with multiple on-device AI models running simultaneously , player detection, ball tracking, and object classification all processing in real time using NCNN with FP16 quantization on standard Android hardware. The same architecture applies to any domain requiring fast, private, offline AI on a mobile device.

What makes us different from a larger agency:
Larger agencies sell you a team and then rotate engineers in and out as priorities shift. You lose context every time someone new joins. With Xandec you work with the same people from discovery through delivery and beyond. I am on every engagement. The engineer who builds your system is the engineer who maintains it. No handovers, no knowledge loss, no surprises six months after launch.

We also tell you the truth before we take your money. If your idea is not technically feasible we say so. If what you want to automate is not worth automating we say that too. The clients who get the most value from Xandec are the ones who want a partner who tells them the truth, not the ones who want someone to start building immediately without asking hard questions first.

description:
['If your email marketing is already generating revenue but you know it should be doing more, I would look at the entire customer journey before adding more emails or campaigns. In many ecommerce brands, the real problem is not the number of emails being sent. It is what happens between the first signup, the first purchase, the second purchase, and the point where a customer becomes inactive.

That is where I come in.

I work with Shopify and ecommerce brands to build and improve email marketing systems that bring more value from the customers and subscribers they already have. That includes Klaviyo, email automation, email communication, segmentation, campaigns, newsletters, and email deliverability - with each part working together instead of operating as seperate pieces.

A recent Klaviyo rebuild generated $29,000 in passive revenue from one automation. Another project helped recover a sender score from 20 to 91 after ongoing inbox placement problems. I have also worked on a system that produced 4.5x email revenue growth in 28 days.

But I do not start by assuming every brand needs more flows.

Sometimes the flows are the problem. Sometimes the segmentation is too basic. Sometimes the campaigns are reaching the wrong people. Sometimes the emails are well designed but never make it into the inbox. And sometimes the account has grown so much that the original setup simply cannot support the customer journey anymore.

What I can help you improve

Email Marketing & Klaviyo

I build and optimise Klaviyo systems around how your customers actually move through the business, including:

• Welcome Series
• Abandoned Cart
• Browse Abandonment
• Post Purchase
• Winback
• VIP and Customer Loyalty
• Replenishment
• Cross-sell and Upsell
• Behaviour-based automations
• Conditional splits and personalised journeys
• Flow audits and full Klaviyo rebuilds

The goal is not to have a long list of flows sitting inside Klaviyo. The goal is to make sure the right customer receives the right communication at the right stage, without your team having to manually manage every interaction.

Email Campaigns & Newsletters

If campaigns are being sent without a clear reason behind them, the list can become tired very quickly.

I can help with campaign planning, email communication, content and copy direction, segmentation, newsletter setup, template design, testing and ongoing campaign execution - so your subscribers are not just receiving more emails, but more relevant reasons to open, click and buy.

Email Deliverability

If your emails suddenly started landing in spam, open rates dropped, or engagement has become difficult to explain, sending more campaigns is usually not the answer.

I work on the technical and behavioural side of email deliverability, including SPF, DKIM and DMARC, sender reputation, domain health, list hygiene, suppression, engagement monitoring and warm-up strategies where needed.

The aim is simple: more of the emails you send should actually reach the people you sent them to.

Segmentation & List Management

Your entire list should not always receive the same message.

I build segments around purchase history, engagement, Shopify behaviour, customer value and lifecycle stage, including VIP, engaged, at-risk, win-back and suppression segments.

This helps you communicate differently with someone who purchased yesterday, someone who has bought five times, and someone who has not opened an email in months.

How I prefer to work

Before building anything, I want to understand what is already happening inside the account.

That means looking at the existing flows, revenue attribution, segmentation, campaign activity, deliverability, customer journey and the gaps between them. From there, we can decide whether you actually need a rebuild, a few targeted fixes, or a completely different email marketing structure.

I also document what is built and why it was built that way. So when the project is finished, you are not left with a Klaviyo account that only the person who built it understands.

If your email marketing currently feels like a collection of campaigns and automations rather than one system working together, send me a message and tell me what is happening now. I will give you a straightforward view of what I would look at first and where I think the biggest opportunity is.Show less']
